query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a minor amount of Sn to a single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based alloy will induce a dual-phase (FCC+BCC) microstructure that increases domain wall pinning and thus overcomes the low coercivity limitation.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy (e.g., FeCoNi or a derivative such as FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8)
generation.intervention: Introduce a minor Sn addition (in the range of 0.02 to 0.10 fraction) during alloy synthesis via vacuum arc-melt casting
generation.conditions: Alloy composition similar to FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8; samples to be annealed at around 673 K to promote phase transformation; measurements conducted at room temperature using standard magnetic characterization techniques
generation.structural_mediator: Induction of a duplex microstructure featuring both FCC and BCC phases, where the BCC phase nucleates preferentially at regions influenced by Sn
generation.mechanism: The slight addition of Sn destabilizes the single-phase fcc structure, promoting the heterogeneous nucleation of a BCC phase. The interfaces between the FCC and newly formed BCC zones act as effective domain wall pinning sites, increasing coercivity by hindering magnetic domain wall motion.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in coercive field relative to the baseline single-phase fcc alloy (which shows coercivity ≤100 Oe); the magnitude of the increase is expected to be significant though the exact value is uncertain.
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi and its matched derivatives have reported coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies for low Sn additions (up to ~10 at% in the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx system) under processing conditions (vacuum arc melting and specific annealing at 673 K) that yield a mixed FCC+BCC phase. Excessive Sn or deviations in processing may lead to unknown phases or inconsistent microstructures.
generation.uncertainty: The precise increase in coercivity is uncertain and depends on achieving the proper balance between the FCC and BCC phases; variability in processing and phase distribution may affect the outcome.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of alloys with the base composition FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 and different levels of Sn addition (e.g., 0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10). Process all samples via identical vacuum arc-melt casting and heat-treatment at 673 K. Characterize the phase structure using X-ray diffraction to confirm the presence of both FCC and BCC phases. Measure the magnetic hysteresis loops at room temperature using a VSM or SQUID magnetometer to determine the coercive fields.
measurements: Magnetic hysteresis loop measurements to extract coercivity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Sn-doped samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in coercivity (i.e., coercivity remains around or below 100 Oe) or if a dual-phase (FCC+BCC) microstructure is not clearly observed, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The present work exhibits the effects of Sn addition on the magnetic properties and microstructure of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The results show all the samples consist of a mixed structure of face-centered-cubic (FCC) phase and body-centered-cubic (BCC) phase. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nano-precipitates in BCC matrix. It also shows that the Curie temperatures (Tc) of the FCC phase and the saturation magnetization (Ms) of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs increase greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases after the addition of Sn into FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA. The thermomagnetic curves indicate that the phases of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs will transform from FCC with low Tc to BCC phase with high Tc at temperature of 600–700 K. This work provides a new idea for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs for their potential application as soft magnets to be used at high temperatures.

In this work, the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs were prepared by vacuum arc-melt casting. Effects of Sn content on the phase constitution and magnetic properties were studied. All the samples are composed of FCC and BCC phases, whereas some unknown phases appear with the addition of Sn. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates in the BCC matrix. Moreover, the Ms increases greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases with the increasing of x for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs. The addition of Sn can obviously increase the Curie temperature of the FCC phase. The phase of alloys with a mixture of FCC and BCC will transform from FCC to BCC phase at high temperature, leading to an increase of magnetization. They can be used as new soft magnetic materials at high temperatures.

reading.lever: Introduce a minor Sn addition to induce a dual-phase (FCC+BCC) microstructure, enhancing domain wall pinning.
reading.why: Because prior evidence indicates that duplex microstructures yield higher coercivity than single-phase FCC, offering a direct pathway to overcome low coercive fields.
